claims.text: Controlled solidification techniques can increase the coercive field of magnetic high-entropy alloys.
Controlled solidification refines the alloy microstructure.
Microstructure refinement improves magnetic domain structure.
Reduction of defects and improvement of magnetic domain structure cause an increase in coercive field.
The coercivity increase should occur at room temperature under standard magnetic testing conditions.
The magnitude or occurrence of the coercivity effect depends on alloy composition and processing conditions.
The matched baseline is an as-cast or annealed alloy made without controlled solidification.
Coercive field and microstructure should be compared between controlled-solidification and conventionally cast samples.
Failure of the controlled-solidification samples to show a significantly higher coercive field than conventionally cast samples would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: Controlled solidification is a fabrication-stage intervention that precedes formation of an as-cast or annealed state, so describing an already as-cast or annealed material as the initial state is temporally ambiguous unless remelting or the complete processing route is specified.
The baseline permits either as-cast or annealed material, whereas the experiment specifies only conventional casting; an annealed comparator would not necessarily be processing-matched.
